source.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
source.authors: Hunar Batra; Lachin Naghashyar; Ashkan Khakzar; P. Torr; Christian Schroeder de Witt; Constantin Venhoff; Ronald Clark

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a different feature-discovery method from the original and causally removes discovered safety-related directions, then reports effects on unsafe-response attack success and VQA performance. It does not test the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original refusal-direction work in related work, but its own safety results concern MMDiff-discovered SAE features, not the original refusal direction. Spatial and OCR interventions are not recorded because they do not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance. Steering results are not recorded as safety results; the reported steering evaluations are for spatial and OCR tasks.
record.test_reason: The study does not test the refusal direction. It ablates SAE features selected because they fire more on unsafe multimodal prompts, and lower attack success follows. These are harmful-content features, not a harmful-minus-harmless direction proposed to mediate refusal. Removing them cutting ASR is neither the effect V1 predicts nor its reverse. Arditi et al. is cited only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that MMDiff finds sparse, causally specific multimodal features: removing them lowers spatial and OCR performance and cuts multimodal ASR by about 24%, with no VQA cost. Steering these features improves spatial and OCR accuracy over single-layer CAA. They note that some safety candidates cause generation collapse rather than refusal and must be filtered out.
record.recipe_differences: Uses warm-started multimodal SAEs, contrastive firing and lexical filtering to discover task-specific features; removes each decoder direction by projection at all layers and text positions. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction or test adding that direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported safety ablations are on PaliGemma 2; the paper says safety and OCR are evaluated on PaliGemma 2 only. The safety features and their effects vary by VLSBench category.

fits_no_version.finding: In PaliGemma 2, ablating single SAE features selected as firing on unsafe image-text prompts cuts VLSBench ASR by 17–28 points per category. The mean over 1,061 candidates is −9.67, with VQA change of about 0 and benign-control change of 1 point or less.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse harmful-content features in VLM backbones causally drive unsafe compliance; removing them increases safe behaviour without capability loss.

record.problems: The safety evaluation is limited to PaliGemma 2. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed safety results. The paper notes that a minority of safety candidates cause generation collapse and require post-hoc filtering. The intervention targets MMDiff-discovered SAE features, not the original refusal direction, limiting how directly the result bears on V1.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant safety rows were left out. Spatial and OCR feature ablations and steering results are omitted because they do not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction is built. No ablation tests whether refusal disappears, and no addition tests whether refusal is induced.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislabelled lowered ASR as 'reversed' for V1. V1 concerns a refusal-mediating direction, whose ablation should raise compliance. These features encode unsafe content, so their removal lowering ASR is a different construct. The limitations section says most effective ablations produce refusal rather than collapse, but this is not quantified. Safety results cover PaliGemma 2 only, with no uncertainty reported. The control rows r13–r18 and r21 are correctly marked none.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not construct the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, test adding a direction, or evaluate a text-only safety-trained chat model. Its relevant intervention is removal of MMDiff-discovered SAE safety features in a multimodal model.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is evaluated.
The study does not test whether jailbreaks suppress a refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
It does not compare affine, cone, single-direction, or multi-direction accounts of refusal.
It does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
It does not test transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Cross-stage ablation concerns spatial features in PaliGemma 2, not how refusal training determines a removable refusal direction.
No reasoning-model refusal-direction experiment is reported.

reader_labels.condition: PaliGemma 2 MMDiff safety-feature ablations on VLSBench unsafe categories and the 1,061-feature sweep
reader_labels.reason: Ablation reduced unsafe-response ASR (r1–r6, r19), rather than increasing harmful compliance as V1 predicts; these are not the original difference-in-means direction.

reader_labels.label: supports
